A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NIMO research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic regression and classification experiments, coefficient-recovery analyses, and evaluations on diabetes and Boston housing data.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds superconductivity experiments, feature-ranking comparisons, and component ablations.

M1.justification: The prediction architecture, feature masking, shared network, and adaptive-ridge/IRLS strategy remain. However, Appendix B.1 Equation 22 and Algorithm 1 add a gamma regularization term to the outer training loss; Appendix B.3 makes a corresponding addition. This is a localized revision of the specified objective beyond renaming profile likelihood as parameter elimination.

E1.justification: v2 adds materials-science regression through superconductivity critical-temperature prediction, extending the real-data applications beyond diabetes and housing. This is a bounded addition within tabular regression. All existing synthetic regression and classification settings remain, including the toy and purely linear examples.

E2.justification: NAM and IMN join the synthetic regression Settings 1–3 and diabetes/Boston performance comparisons, while Contextual Lasso disappears from the synthetic regression comparison. SHAP applied to NIMO becomes an additional reference for feature rankings in v2 Table 2. The classification comparator set remains logistic regression, NN, and LassoNet.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an interpretability evaluation design using MEM-based feature rankings across models and comparison with global SHAP rankings. It also introduces controlled masked/unmasked and positional-encoding configurations for ablation. Existing synthetic 200/100/100 and real-data 60%/20%/20% split designs remain; the substantial change is in the added evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's coefficient recovery, linear sanity check, and sparsity illustrations, v2 directly tests component necessity. Section 4.3 and Appendix D.5 compare masked inputs with positional encoding, unmasked inputs with encoding, and unmasked inputs without encoding across three synthetic settings (Figures 7, 15, and 16). MEM/SHAP ranking comparisons also add analysis of agreement between explanations on real data.

E5.justification: v1 consistently reports five independent real-data splits. v2 Section 4.2 reports nine seeds for diabetes and Boston housing and five for superconductivity, but Appendix D.4 still states five runs for all datasets. The reported repetition counts therefore change, although the actual increase is unresolved. Reporting variability across splits is retained.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises NIMO's Settings 1–3 MSEs from 0.030/0.217/0.334 to 0.024/0.197/0.380; LassoNet's Settings 2–3 values change from 2.991/1.342 to 2.612/1.738. NAM/IMN scores, superconductivity outcomes, feature rankings, and ablation findings are newly reported. Toy-example and vanilla-regression MSE entries disappear, although those settings remain elsewhere. Classification accuracies are unchanged in v2 Table 3. These are reported result revisions, not uniformly improved performance.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.2 formally defines ME and MEM and derives NIMO's input derivative, including cross-feature terms, establishing MEM_j = beta_j at the standardized mean. Appendix B also revises the elimination objectives to retain gamma regularization. These refine the existing mathematical framework; the adaptive-ridge and sub-l1 arguments remain. A new inconsistency persists: Equation 22 squares the gamma norm, whereas Algorithm 1 and Equation 32 do not.

C1.justification: The central promise of expressive nonlinear prediction with interpretable coefficients remains. v2 explicitly frames global interpretability through MEM and emphasizes faithful feature effects and per-instance explanations. Its abstract replaces v1's broad higher-performance assertion with good predictive performance, refining the headline claims without replacing the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations connecting low-data robustness to regularization and optimization, interpreting masking/encoding ablations, and discussing MEM/SHAP ranking disagreements. It also identifies feature correlations as an obstacle to clear sparsity on superconductivity. The specific v1 suggestion that Boston feature B's apparent importance arose from linear-model artifacts is removed. Highly nonlinear and self-interaction limitations remain, relocated to the conclusion.

D1.justification: v2 adds NAM/IMN implementation sources and settings, explicitly describes lasso/group-penalty grid search, and changes reported hardware from RTX 2080 Ti to RTX 5080. Conversely, it omits v1's three-layer specification, Gaussian-noise scale 0.2, first-layer tanh detail, and regression/classification output ranges. The detailed logistic Algorithm 2 is removed while its derivation remains. These documentation changes do not establish that the omitted components were abandoned.

R1.justification: The research positioning shifts substantially toward feature effects, marginal effects, and the fidelity limitations of post-hoc explanations, supported by new references such as Nguyen and Scholbeck et al. Section 2 expands the hybrid comparison to NAM and IMN and removes the detailed Contextual Lasso discussion. Contextual Lasso remains cited elsewhere, so its removal from experiments is distinct from citation removal.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, interpretability discussion, optimization explanation, experiments, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Experiments are reorganized around methods/protocol and three hypotheses, followed by ablations. The toy example moves into the method section; classification, detailed real-data discussion, and group-sparsity material move into appendices; limitations are incorporated into the conclusion.

P2.justification: Table 1 is transposed and reduced, and the classification table moves to the appendix. Real-data performance and coefficient plots are reorganized into separate main-text figures with updated composite figures in the appendix. v2 adds a highlighted ranking table and superconductivity/ablation figures. The title treatment, section typography, running headers, and page layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1's mainly illustrative coefficient analyses, v2 makes the interpretability claims more assessable through explicit ME/MEM equations and direct masking/encoding ablations. NAM/IMN comparisons also provide useful additional context. These support a modest net improvement, but conflicting five-versus-nine run counts, inconsistent gamma-penalty formulas, and lost implementation details limit the gain in scientific reliability and reproducibility.
